hero.eyebrow: Solidity · Every code sample compiled and checked
hero.title: Solidity for Beginners: read it, reason about it, design it
hero.subtitle: Work through complete example contracts from types to a full crowdfunding project, classify and review code, calculate gas and write specifications and tests plans. Examples were compiled with Solidity 0.8; you try them in the free Remix editor.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can read most simple contracts, write small ones with safe patterns and review code for common bugs.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.
Complete the escrow design and the final assessment.

faq.q: Does the platform compile or run my Solidity?
faq.a: No. The course labs check your reading, analysis and design work. You run and edit the examples yourself in Remix, a free browser tool, and the lessons explain how.
Some basic idea of variables and functions helps, but the lessons explain every construct used.

faq.q: Is the code safe to deploy?
faq.a: The examples are for learning. Anything holding real value should be tested far more and professionally audited.

activities.title: How big can an integer be?
activities.objective: Work out the largest value for each unsigned integer size and see why uint256 is so big.
activities.scenario: A uint of n bits can hold values from 0 to 2^n minus 1. Smaller sizes can save storage when packed together, but they overflow sooner.
steps: In C2 work out 2 to the power of the bits in B2 with POWER.
In D2 work out the largest value: C2 minus 1.
Fill down rows 2 to 6.
In B9 show Too small if the largest uint8 value (D2) is less than 1,000, using IF.

checks.label: C2 is 2^8
checks.hint: =POWER(2,B2)
checks.explain: Two to the number of bits.

checks.label: D2 is 255
checks.hint: Try the formula =C2-1 here.
checks.explain: The largest value is one less.

checks.label: D4 is the largest uint32
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: B9 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(D2<1000,"Too small","Fine")

activities.title: What does a loop cost?
activities.objective: Compare looping over an array with a direct mapping lookup in gas, and see why unbounded loops are dangerous.
activities.scenario: Reading a storage slot for the first time in a transaction costs about 2,100 gas. Looping over n items reads n slots. A mapping lookup reads one. The block gas limit is about 30 million. (Teaching figures.)
steps: In C2 work out the gas of looping over n items: n times the cost per read (B8).
In D2 work out the gas of one mapping lookup: just the cost per read.
In E2 work out how many times more the loop costs: C2 divided by D2.
Fill down rows 2 to 6.
In B10 work out the largest n that fits in a block: the block limit (B9) divided by the cost per read, rounded down with INT.

checks.label: C2 is the loop cost for 10
D2 is one lookup
checks.hint: Try the formula =$B$8 here.

checks.label: E2 is the ratio
C6 is the loop cost for 100,000
checks.hint: Fill down.
checks.explain: 210 million gas, far over the limit.

checks.label: B10 is the largest n
checks.hint: =INT(B9/B8)
checks.explain: The block limit divided by the read cost.

cells.E1: Loop costs this many times more
cells.A10: Largest n that fits in one block

activities.title: Review a contract for bugs
activities.objective: Find and explain problems in a contract described in words, and say how to fix each.
activities.scenario: A student's Raffle contract works like this: anyone calls enter() with exactly 0.1 ETH; the owner calls pickWinner(), which chooses the winner using block.timestamp modulo the number of players, then sends the whole balance to the winner with transfer-style code that ignores whether the send worked, and only afterwards clears the players array. The owner can call pickWinner at any time, even with one player. Review it.
steps: Add Heading 2 sections: Problems, Fixes.
Under Problems list at least four issues in bullets.
Under Fixes write a numbered list of at least four fixes matching them.
Mention randomness and the ignored result of sending ETH.
Keep it between 120 and 280 words.

activities.title: The numbers behind a crowdfund
activities.objective: Calculate progress, the funding verdict and refunds for a Crowdfund campaign.
activities.scenario: A campaign has a goal of 5 ETH. Backers pledged the amounts below. Work out progress, whether it succeeded, and what each backer gets back if it fails. (Amounts in ETH.)
steps: In B8 total the pledges with SUM.
In B9 work out the progress: raised divided by the goal.
In B10 show Funded if raised is at least the goal, else Refund.
In C2 work out each backer's share of the total raised: pledge divided by raised. Fill down.
In D2 work out each backer's refund if the campaign failed: their pledge if B10 is Refund, otherwise 0. Fill down.

checks.label: B8 is the total
checks.hint: =SUM(B2:B5)

checks.label: B9 is the progress
B10 is Refund
checks.hint: =IF(B8>=B7,"Funded","Refund")

checks.label: C2 is Asha's share
D4 is Chitra's refund
checks.hint: =IF($B$10="Refund",B4,0)
checks.explain: A refund equals the pledge when the goal failed.

activities.title: Final project: design an Escrow contract
activities.objective: Design, specify and review a complete small contract before writing any code.
activities.scenario: Design an Escrow contract: a buyer deposits ETH for a seller, the buyer releases the money when happy, the seller can refund the buyer, and if neither acts within 14 days an arbiter chosen at deployment decides.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Escrow: design document'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Purpose, State, Functions, Events and errors, Security review, Tests.
Under State list at least five variables with their types in bullets.
Under Functions list at least five functions with who may call each.
Under Security review mention reentrancy and checks-effects-interactions.
Under Tests write a numbered list of at least six tests including failures.
Keep it between 260 and 520 words.
